summary: No release-blocking issue found. The search term is passed as a bound parameter, the sort order comes from a fixed allowlist of SQL fragments, and the page offset is clamped.

No code defect was identified, but the audit result omits the mandatory critical payment-verification check, so the evidence is incomplete and release_gate.py returns NO-GO. The team's GO is not supported.

GET /projects trusts the client-supplied x-org-id header and never checks it against the authenticated user's orgIds, so any signed-in user can list another organisation's projects and budgets (cross-tenant IDOR, CWE-639). Authorise the org against res.locals.user.orgIds on the server.

No release-blocking issue found. RLS is enabled with owner-scoped select, insert, update, and delete policies (the update USING clause also acts as WITH CHECK), anon access is revoked, so the unscoped client update can only affect the caller's own notes.

The one open finding is a medium one: login has no per-account rate limit (AG-007). It is accepted with a named owner, an approver, a date, and a reason. All mandatory checks have runtime evidence on the release commit, so release_gate.py returns CONDITIONAL GO, not the GO the team claimed.

DELETE /api/internal/users/[id] is outside the /api/admin middleware matcher and only calls requireSession, so any authenticated member can permanently delete any user account (missing function-level authorisation, CWE-285). Enforce the admin role in the route handler itself, and do not rely on the middleware alone for the admin routes.

No release-blocking issue found. The webhook verifies the Stripe signature, grants the plan only when payment_status is paid (also handling async_payment_succeeded), and records the event id idempotently in the same transaction as the update.

The webhook grants the pro plan on checkout.session.completed without checking payment_status, but Bacs Direct Debit and bank-transfer (customer_balance) checkouts complete while still unpaid, so users get paid access without paying. It also ignores async_payment_succeeded/failed, and the check-then-insert deduplication is not atomic and is written before processing succeeds.

The avatar import checks the URL with a string startsWith prefix, which accepts hosts like https://images.partner-cdn.com.attacker.example or userinfo tricks, and it then follows redirects. That lets an authenticated user make the server fetch internal or metadata URLs (SSRF, CWE-918). There is also no size or content-type validation on the stored bytes.

AG-004, a confirmed high-severity finding (password reset tokens never expire), is marked accepted. High findings cannot be accepted, so release_gate.py returns NO-GO until it is fixed and verified on the release commit.

The critical ownership check was recorded on commit 7fd543e, before the change to the invoice lookup in src/routes.py, so its evidence is stale for the release commit. release_gate.py returns NO-GO until the check is re-run on HEAD.

The SECURITY DEFINER function document_preview bypasses RLS and returns the title and the first 280 characters of the body for any document id, with no owner check. Any authenticated user (and anon, through the default PUBLIC execute grant) can read other users' documents. Add an owner_id = auth.uid() filter or use SECURITY INVOKER, and revoke execute from public/anon.

release_gate.py prints GO, but the critical ownership, tenant-isolation, and payment-verification PASSes were recorded with the commands 'true' and 'echo tenant isolation verified'. Those commands test nothing, so these critical controls are unverified, and I would record NO-GO until real tests are run on the release commit (ideally in CI with --ci-evidence).

The transfer view accepts any Decimal amount without checking that it is positive and finite. A negative amount passes the funds check and moves money from the recipient to the sender, which lets a user drain other wallets (CWE-20/CWE-840). Validate amount > 0, a finite value, and the allowed precision before the transfer.
The critical tenant-isolation check is marked PASS on static evidence only (reading the code), and critical controls need runtime evidence. release_gate.py returns NO-GO.

No release-blocking issue found. The invoice lookup goes through a Prisma extension that forces userId from the session into findFirst/findMany, so the route returns 404 for another user's invoice. As defence in depth, extend the scoping to the other query methods.

createCheckout spreads the client-supplied line input over the server product data (...input after unitAmount and name), so a customer can send their own unitAmount and name and pay any price (client-trusted price, CWE-602). Build the line from server values only, and copy just the validated quantity and note.
